featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Mangal Murti Hall in Bhayandar East is a well-known budget-friendly venue for weddings, engagements, and family functions. Here is a detailed review based on local feedback and venue specifications.
Overview & Capacity
Located near Bharat Bank and Gandhi Udyan Circle, this venue has been serving the Bhayandar community for over 14–20 years. It typically features a two-floor layout that can be used independently or together.
* Seating Capacity: Approximately 250 to 400 guests.
* Floating Capacity: Can accommodate up to 600 guests.
* Food Type: Strictly Pure Vegetarian.
Good Sides
* Budget-Friendly: One of the most affordable options in the area, with veg plate prices starting around ₹350. It is ideal for families looking for a functional venue without a luxury price tag.
* Strategic Location: It is very easy to find and commute to, being close to major landmarks like Goddev Naka and Bharat Bank.
* Flexible Space: The availability of two halls allows for separate areas for the main ceremony and dining, or for hosting smaller events like birthdays and "Godh Bharai" (baby showers).
* Supportive Staff: Many locals mention that the management and staff are cooperative and helpful during the event setup.
Bad Sides
* Air Conditioning Issues: While some listings mention AC, many local reviews point out that the cooling can be insufficient for a large crowd, making it uncomfortable during hot summer months.
* Hygiene & Maintenance: The washrooms and changing rooms are frequently cited as areas needing improvement. They can be small and are not always maintained to a high standard of cleanliness during busy events.
* Parking Constraints: Although there is dedicated parking for about 30–40 vehicles, it can get very chaotic during peak wedding season as the surrounding roads are quite busy.
* Strict Policies: They generally do not allow outside caterers or DJs, which limits your options if you have a specific preference for food or entertainment.
Final Summary & Conclusion
Shree Mangal Murti Hall is a solid choice for middle-class families and those planning medium-sized functions (200–400 people) on a budget. It excels in providing a central location and decent vegetarian food at a competitive price.
Conclusion: If you are planning a grand, high-end wedding, this might feel too basic. However, for a traditional, simple ceremony where cost-effectiveness and location are the priorities, it is one of the most reliable halls in Bhayandar East.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sure! Here's an example of a fake, exaggerated, and sarcastic review for a hall:

"The Hall of Legends"

If you're looking for a hall that combines space, mystery, and a complete lack of anything remotely helpful, this is the place for you!

Location and Accessibility:
The hall is so "conveniently" located, you’ll have plenty of time to question your life choices on your way there. Finding parking? A fun scavenger hunt! It's right next to a busy street, so you can enjoy the sounds of traffic while trying to have a conversation. If you’re brave enough to navigate public transport, it’s just far enough away to make you rethink your decision the minute you step off the bus. But hey, at least it's accessible, right?

Size and Layout:
The hall’s size is “impressive” — you’ll wonder if they even know how to fill such a vast space. The seating is arranged in a way that feels like a game of "guess where the best view is." There’s no clear direction; it’s more of a free-for-all. If you’re hosting an event, good luck finding a spot that doesn’t make you feel like you’re sitting in the back row of a cinema.

Facilities and Equipment:
The equipment? Oh, it’s “top-notch” if by top-notch, you mean it worked half the time. The sound system has a mind of its own — sometimes you hear everything, other times, it's like playing hide-and-seek with your own voice. The projectors, if they decide to cooperate, are a sight to behold. As for lighting? It’s either too bright or too dim. There's no in-between.

Customer Service and Staff:
The staff is “incredibly” helpful, assuming you enjoy waiting for 20 minutes to be acknowledged. Once they do decide to help, they’ll “guide” you with all the enthusiasm of a person who’s just been told they’re working overtime. Any inquiries? Expect a response somewhere between tomorrow and never.

Event Management:
Event coordination? Absolutely. If you consider random assignments, unexplained delays, and a sudden sense of panic event management. But if chaos is your thing, then they’ve got you covered. Need a catering service? Prepare yourself for mystery food — it’s always a surprise. Will it be edible? Who knows!

Ambiance and Atmosphere:
The ambiance is a "dream" — if that dream involves forgetting what normal lighting feels like. The decor is just there to remind you that this hall has tried to be modern, but somehow, the 90s still hold on. The space is huge, which is great unless you’re stuck in the middle and the AC is doing its best impression of a ceiling fan. It’s the perfect temperature — either freezing cold or boiling hot.

Pricing and Packages:
Pricing is “competitive.” What does that mean? It means you’ll pay an arm and a leg for a hall that could definitely use some TLC. The packages are “flexible” if you consider getting the least for the most. Looking for a discount? That’s cute.

User Experience and Feedback:
If you like hearing people grumble about how they’ll never book again, you’ll love the feedback. It’s mostly positive, because most guests are too polite to say anything outright. When the event's over, people are left trying to remember if they had a good time or were just grateful to leave.

Strengths and Weaknesses:
Strengths? Well, the hall is huge, which is a plus if you’re into open spaces. Weaknesses? Everything else. It’s got the charm of an outdated office building, the service of a forgotten ghost town, and the ambiance of an overly enthusiastic party with too many flashing lights.

Conclusion:
In conclusion, this hall is perfect for people who enjoy the thrill of unpredictability. If you love the idea of spending a lot for the chance of something going wrong, this place is calling your name. Would I recommend it? Only if you’re after a one-of-a-kind experience in disappointment. Otherwise, keep looking.

featured_reviews.name: Vinay Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had pre booked the facility 4 months in advance for my brother’s wedding, for 500 pax. On the day of the wedding food was delayed by 45mins to an hour. At 11.30 we were informed that there is some issue with the gas burners. Imagine our shock and surprise. Wedding got over at 10.30-45am. Still we somehow managed the crowd till 12 noon, but food was not ready and we got to know they had just started preparing food sometime back.

Can you imagine the level of mismanagement and carelessness. For such an important function in our live we were half the time following up and arguing with them. And after 12 the female staff from the office came into the kitchen and started directing the staff.
Food was getting ready one by one at 12.30 when the feast should have started latest by 12. Guests had already gathered at the 2nd floor banquet by 11.45.

Finally one counter was opened at around 12.50pm that too without few items we had decided up on. There was commotion and long queues due to single counter. Next counter was opened at around 1.20pm.

I generally don’t write reviews, especially bad ones unless it’s absolutely necessary so that nobody else faces the same plight that we went through. Me and the parents were almost in tears because of the situation because crowd had gathered for food and we we were just saying 5 mins -10 mins everytime. It was the most embarrassing situation caused by casual and irresponsible people at Shri Balaji Banquet.

The real problem:

Multiple events taking place without proper planning: There was a baby naming ceremony on the 3rd floor, meaning food had to be prepared for both events. Who will plan for this???

Food order given to 3rd party: We were given Mr. Pankaj’s nimber for cordination but when things went south he said he’s a vendor and that the banquet management is responsible for this. He shared the owner’s number.

Spoke to Mr. Amit Sharma. No satisfactory response, No sorry, nothing. I still have the chats record. Zero response to my 100 messages. He just answered one call after multiple attempts to tell me that he will check. That’s it!

Our mistake: We made 100% payment upfront and that was a forced rule by the banquet management.

We trusted the wrong people.

Also there is only 1 small lift for the entire facility which is a huge hindrance especially for elderly and children and if there is another event that day then it’s gonna be a nightmare.

Final advice: If you want to waste your money and spoil your reputation and peace of mind then only book with them.

Hope this review helps atleast 1 person to escape our plight.

Thank you🙏🏼
